## Answer key for practice_01

Try `practice_01.Rmd` on your own before you look at these!

```{r}
options(scipen=999)
library(tidyverse)

contracts <- read_csv("data/contracts_wide.csv")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Q1.** Which Knicks (`NYK`) players make more than \$20 million in 2026-27? Who's the highest-paid Knick?

```{r}
knicks_20m <- contracts |>
  filter(team == "NYK" & salary_2026_27 > 20000000) |>
  select(player, team, salary_2026_27) |>
  arrange(desc(salary_2026_27))

knicks_20m
```

**A1.** Five Knicks make more than \$20 million: Karl-Anthony Towns, OG Anunoby, Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart. Towns is the highest paid at \$57,078,728.

*Common mistake: writing `team = "NYK"` with one equals sign. Inside `filter()` you need `==`, which asks "is this equal?" A single `=` tries to assign a value instead.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Q2.** Sort every player into a pay tier, then count the players and find the average salary in each tier.

```{r}
pay_tiers <- contracts |>
  filter(multi_team_entry == FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    pay_tier = case_when(
      salary_2026_27 >= 40000000 ~ "Star",
      salary_2026_27 >= 15000000 ~ "Starter",
      salary_2026_27 >= 5000000 ~ "Role player",
      TRUE ~ "Minimum"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(pay_tier) |>
  summarise(
    players = n(),
    avg_salary = mean(salary_2026_27)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(players))

pay_tiers
```

**A2.** "Minimum" is the biggest tier, with 209 players averaging about \$2.7 million. Only 44 players are "Stars," but they average about \$48.4 million each, roughly 18 times what a minimum player makes. Most of the league is paid close to the bottom, while a small group at the top takes in a huge share of the money.

*Why the order inside `case_when()` matters: R checks each line from top to bottom and stops at the first one that's true. Because the \$40M check comes first, a \$45M player is labeled "Star" before R ever reaches the \$15M line. `TRUE ~ "Minimum"` at the end catches everyone left over.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Q3.** How many players have "Jr." in their name, and which team has the most of them? How much are those players paid in 2026-27 for each team?

```{r}
jr_players <- contracts |>
  filter(str_detect(player, fixed("Jr.")))

nrow(jr_players)

jr_players |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    jr_players = n(),
    total_salary = sum(salary_2026_27)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(jr_players))
```

**A3.** 23 players have "Jr." in their name. Milwaukee has the most, with 3, who are paid \$26,529,841 combined in 2026-27. Brooklyn has only 2, but they're paid the most combined: \$49,593,150.

*The trap: try `str_detect(player, "Jr.")` without `fixed()`. You get 24 rows instead of 23. In `str_detect()`, a period means "any character," so "Jr." also matches the "Jru" in **Jrue Holiday**. `fixed()` tells R to look for the exact characters you typed.*

```{r}
# See the extra match for yourself
contracts |>
  filter(str_detect(player, "Jr.") & !str_detect(player, fixed("Jr."))) |>
  select(player, team)
```
